headline: Nasdaq-100: the Iran sanctions announcement printed without an oil spike, so Tail eases to the low band while Stress stays elevated on the memory de-rating
body:
The event that shaped the last three hours of assessment has resolved. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Operation Economic Outcast at the 17:00Z press conference, an expanded sanctions campaign against Iran's financial system spanning digital assets, gold, aviation, technology and shipping, with broadened secondary sanctions on entities that transact with Tehran and a stated intent to remove facilitators from the US dollar system. CBS News reports the measures as newly imposed rather than merely threatened, while CNN's live coverage notes the Treasury stopped short of large new penalties on the third countries it warned.

What matters for a Nasdaq-100 risk assessment is not the severity of the language but whether the announcement created a supply discontinuity that transmits into equities through energy. It did not. WTI is 84.82 dollars, down 2.57% on the day, and Brent is 92.07 dollars, down 2.46%. Oil extended its pre-announcement decline rather than reversing, which removes the specific amplifier that kept the danger window open through the afternoon.

Equity price action across the announcement is orderly and two-way. The Nasdaq-100 cash index is 29,069.45, down 0.82%, at 17:26Z on Investing.com real-time data. That is about 74 points below the 29,143.52 session high reached in the prior hour and about 194 points above the 28,875.97 low, so the index has given back part of a recovery inside a range it has now traded in both directions. NQ futures are 29,160.75 at 17:05Z inside a 28,948.00-29,480.50 day range. Neither series shows the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that Tail measures.

Volatility confirms the reading. VIX is 15.75, up 4.10% on the day but sitting near the bottom of a 15.61-16.06 range, and delayed Finviz context has VIX futures 0.58% lower. Cross-assets are not aligned with a liquidation: the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.70%, 3.3 basis points lower, the 2-year is 4.24% and effectively unchanged, and delayed Treasury futures context shows the curve bid with the 30-year contract up 0.75%.

The weakness in the index remains narrow and thematic rather than systemic. Delayed latest-session Finviz context shows technology down 1.36% while communication services is up 1.15%, semiconductors down 2.71% and software roughly flat. All seven tracked semiconductors are lower, led by Micron at -5.4%, after the report that Nvidia will raise AI-server prices by more than 15% in early 2027 because of memory costs. Five of eight megacaps are higher, with Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet all positive. The Dow is up 0.12% while the S&P 500 is down 0.27% and the Nasdaq Composite down 0.54%. Dispersion of that kind supplies the two-way trade a mean-reversion basket depends on.

One genuinely new item entered the tape today. President Trump said tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel will rise to 50% from 1 January 2027 after weekend talks collapsed, and Prime Minister Carney has retaliatory duties scheduled for next month. The immediate equity effect has been in automakers rather than the Nasdaq-100, but it is a live escalation that belongs in the Stress reading.

Tail is scored at 9. The single pending catalyst resolved without the price path that would threaten mean reversion, volatility is decaying and cross-assets are stable. Stress eases to 46 from 50 as the event component clears, but stays elevated on the memory de-rating, the tariff escalation, an unresolved Strait of Hormuz closure and Wednesday's stack of Core PCE, the second GDP estimate, Durable Goods and Nvidia's results after the close. The danger window is reset to 19:00Z-20:00Z, covering the power hour into the cash close, which is the session's only remaining scheduled checkpoint.

The 24-hour conditional path stays inside the low Tail band throughout, rising to 11 in the power hour, easing overnight to a 8-12 range with the highest overnight reading at the 00:00Z Tokyo and Seoul opens where the memory complex is priced directly, and building again through Tuesday to 16 at the 14:00Z US cash open, where CB Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales print together. Confidence is 88: live cash and futures quotes, a live volatility reading, current yields and oil, a verified event outcome and Finviz context collected eight minutes before the assessment are all in hand.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Through the 23 August evening Tail was pinned at 4 with the EA_ON mapping while Stress drifted from 40 to 45 in a normal mode. Tail stepped to 15 at 22:00Z as the Asian technology decline began, then settled into a 7-12 band overnight. It rose to 19 at 07:00Z with Stress at 58, the window's highest, as the European session priced the memory complex lower in a trend-down mode, eased to 11-13 in a mixed mode through the European morning, moved to 20 at 13:00Z with the cash open pending, and reached 26 at 14:00Z, the only slot in the window mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES, when the index sat near its low with a single shallow pullback. It fell to 13 at 15:00Z as that structure failed and the retracement began, and to 10 at 16:00Z once the opening decline was fully retraced. The window therefore contains one orange slot and one yellow slot inside an otherwise green series, and the elevated reading was resolved by observed mean reversion rather than by extension.
outlookSummary: The conditional path holds the low Tail band across all 24 hours. It stays at 9 into 18:00Z, lifts to 11 for the 19:00Z power hour that carries the danger window, and eases to 10 at the 20:00Z cash close. The evening floor is 8 at 21:00Z, with the overnight series in an 8-12 range and the highest overnight reading of 12 at 00:00Z, where the Tokyo and Seoul opens price the memory-cost story directly. It returns to 8 at the 05:00Z inter-session gap, lifts to 11 at the 07:00Z European cash open, which was the weakest hour of the preceding window, and eases through the European morning. The series then builds to 13 at 13:00Z with Case-Shiller pending and 16 at 14:00Z, the highest conditional slot, where the Tuesday US cash open coincides with CB Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales, before easing to 14 and 12. Conditional Stress peaks at 51 in that opening hour and troughs at 39 overnight. Confidence declines from 88 to 75 across the horizon as the forecast moves beyond currently observed evidence.
